nodes.body: `span64` is still cast to `unsigned` for `pipe_buffer_map_range`, but the new guard doesn’t reject `span64 > UINT_MAX` or `offset+span` overflowing 32-bit. If `span64` fits in the BO size but exceeds `UINT_MAX`, or if `offset + span64` exceeds `UINT_MAX`, the `(unsigned)` casts can truncate/wrap and map the wrong range (potentially OOB). Add explicit `UINT_MAX`/overflow checks before the cast.

The new `vkCmdFillBuffer` guard checks `offset/size <= UINT_MAX`, but it doesn’t prevent 32-bit `offset + size` overflow in the `pipe_buffer_map_range` call. With a large (>4GiB) VkBuffer, `offset` and `size` can each be <= `UINT_MAX` while `offset + size` exceeds `UINT_MAX`, and the internal unsigned addition can wrap. Add an explicit `offset > UINT_MAX - size` check (after `size > UINT_MAX`).

`vkCmdCopyBuffer2` still casts `cb->size` to `unsigned` before validating it. The new bounds check rejects regions past the VkDeviceSize buffer, but it doesn’t reject `cb->size > UINT_MAX` (truncation) or `src_offset + size` / `dst_offset + size` exceeding 32-bit (unsigned wrap inside `pipe_buffer_map_range`). Add explicit `cb->size > UINT_MAX` and `offset > UINT_MAX - cb->size` checks to ensure the cast/map range is representable in Gallium’s `unsigned` API.

`vkCmdUpdateBuffer` still computes `unsigned size = (unsigned)ub->size` before ensuring `ub->size` is representable in Gallium’s `unsigned` length, and it doesn’t prevent 32-bit `offset + size` overflow (wrap) in `pipe_buffer_map_range`. Add explicit checks for `ub->size > UINT_MAX` and `ub->offset > UINT_MAX - ub->size` before mapping.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clamp indexed vertex fetches against vertex buffers**

When robustBufferAccess is advertised, an indexed draw can still fetch attributes past the bound vertex buffers: this only limits `draw.count` to the number of index elements inside the index buffer, unlike the non-indexed path which calls `r300vk_robust_vertex_count()` over the vertex bindings. A valid robust-buffer test with a small vertex buffer and an in-range index buffer containing a large index (plus `vertexOffset`) will pass this clamp and let Gallium/r300 read the out-of-bounds vertex attribute instead of preventing the access.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Compute gl_VertexIndex from fetched indices**

When an indexed draw uses a VS that reads `gl_VertexIndex`, this path builds the synthetic system-value stream from `firstIndex + i` before the index buffer is processed, so shaders see the ordinal index position rather than the fetched index value plus `vertexOffset`. This affects the SW-TCL path where system values are supplied as vertex inputs, and it will render indexed draws/tests that depend on `gl_VertexIndex` incorrectly.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind the UBO selected by the shader**

When a pipeline layout has an earlier UBO binding that the shader does not read and the shader's single UBO is a later `(set, binding)`, this accepts that later binding but discards which binding was seen; replay still calls `r300vk_bind_descriptor_ubo()`, which scans descriptor sets and binds the first UBO it finds to `CONST[0]`. That makes a valid single-UBO shader read the wrong buffer whenever the layout contains another UBO before the one actually referenced.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore a real NULL DSA state**

When a still-bound DSA CSO is destroyed, this clears `r300->dsa_state.state`, so the next r300 blitter operation saves NULL and later restores it via `bind_depth_stencil_alpha_state(NULL)`. I checked `r300_bind_dsa_state()`, and it returns immediately for NULL instead of updating the atom, which leaves the blitter's internal DSA CSO bound after the clear/copy rather than restoring the no-DSA state the delete path just installed.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Indexed draws currently produce incorrect gl_VertexIndex values when the pipeline needs the synthetic vertex-id stream. r300vk_bind_synthetic_index_stream fills the stream with a linear sequence (base+i), but for vkCmdDrawIndexed gl_VertexIndex must be (index_buffer[firstIndex+i] + vertexOffset). Leaving this as a TODO means shaders reading gl_VertexIndex will silently render incorrect results for indexed draws.

The indexed-draw path casts start_elem (uint64) to unsigned for draw.start without any bounds check. If index_offset/first_index produce a start_elem > UINT_MAX, this truncates and can make draw fetch indices from the wrong place (and potentially past the end of the CPU-mapped index buffer on the SW-TCL path). This file already guards other pipe_* unsigned offset casts elsewhere; the indexed draw path should similarly fail closed when start_elem is not representable.

r300vk_index_type_bytes returns 2 for unknown VkIndexType values. That can cause the driver to interpret unexpected index types (e.g., VK_INDEX_TYPE_NONE_KHR) as 16-bit indices, leading to incorrect range calculations and potentially out-of-bounds element reads during replay. Prefer a fail-closed mapping (0 bytes for NONE/unknown), or use vk_index_type_to_bytes() which already handles NONE and validates types.

CmdDrawIndexed snapshots cmd->bound_index_* state, but r300vk_cmd_buffer_reset_recording_state() doesn't clear these newly added fields. Since other bound state (pipelines, current_color_image) is reset there, leaving bound_index_* intact is inconsistent and can lead to stale index-buffer state being reused across a BeginCommandBuffer/reset cycle if a recording forgets to bind an index buffer (or binds VK_NULL_HANDLE).

The failure message for r300vk_nir_lower_vulkan_resource_index_single is misleading. The pass returns false for any vulkan_resource_index whose descriptor type is not nir_descriptor_type_uniform_buffer (e.g., sampled images/samplers), but the error string only mentions storage buffers / multiple UBOs / dynamic UBO index and frames it purely as a constant-file limitation. Please update the message to reflect that only a single UBO descriptor is supported and other descriptor types are rejected too.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve HOST_COHERENT readback without invalidate**

When a linear image is bound after the allocation was already mapped, this path keeps the host pointer on the lazy buffer and only refreshes it from the image tile in `vkInvalidateMappedMemoryRanges`. However memory type 0 is advertised as `HOST_VISIBLE | HOST_COHERENT`, so a valid readback can copy into the linear image, wait for completion, and read the mapped pointer without calling invalidate; in that case the pointer still sees the stale lazy buffer instead of the copied image contents. The binding path needs to make the mapped storage coherent with the image tile without relying on invalidate-only synchronization, or stop exposing this as coherent host-visible memory for this case.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Copy image data relative to the mapped range**

For map-before-bind linear images with a nonzero bind offset, this writes to `map_ptr + memory_offset`, but `map_ptr` is the pointer returned by `vkMapMemory` for the caller's mapped range, not necessarily the base of the whole allocation. If an app maps only the suballocated image range at the same nonzero offset before binding, invalidate copies the tile past the returned mapping and leaves the bytes the app will read unchanged (or overruns the mapped range). The image sync path needs to account for the map offset, as well as the bind offset, before adding to `map_ptr`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Cap linear image properties to the creatable size**

Advertising nonzero linear-tiling transfer features makes `vkGetPhysicalDeviceImageFormatProperties2` report the generic 2D max extent of 4096x4096 for linear images, but `r300vk_CreateImage` rejects any linear dimension above `R300VK_R3XX_MAX_RENDER_DIMENSION` (2560). Apps that correctly query a 4096-wide linear transfer image will be told it is supported and then get `VK_ERROR_FORMAT_NOT_SUPPORTED` at create time, so the linear query path needs a 2560 cap or the create gate must match the advertised properties.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject non-2D linear images in format queries**

For linear tiling this create gate rejects every image type except 2D, but `vkGetPhysicalDeviceImageFormatProperties2` now sees the nonzero linear transfer features and still reports success for 1D and 3D transfer images in its existing type switch. A caller that queries a linear 1D/3D staging image can therefore receive supported properties and then fail at `vkCreateImage`; the image-format query needs to apply the same linear-only-2D restriction.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

BindImageMemory2 sets bound_image_tile/bound_image_row_pitch for the map-before-bind linear case, but it never clears mem->bound_resource (and it also leaves any previous bound_image_tile/row_pitch state in place for other paths). Since InvalidateMappedMemoryRanges always runs both r300vk_sync_owns_buffer and r300vk_sync_owns_image, stale bindings can trigger an unintended extra sync (and potentially overwrite the host map with unrelated buffer contents before the image pull). Clear the non-applicable binding state when binding an image so only the active binding participates in Flush/Invalidate sync.

nodes.body: `nir_imm_float(b, 0.0)` always creates an f32 constant. If `nir_op_imod` is ever used at a non-32-bit size, this will produce mismatched bit-sizes in `nir_flt`/`nir_bcsel`, yielding invalid NIR. Use a bit-size-matched immediate instead.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Guard zero divisors before float lowering**

When any newly handled `udiv`/`umod`/`irem`/`imod` has a zero divisor, the NIR opcode contracts return 0 (checked in `src/compiler/nir/nir_opcodes.py` via `rg --fixed-strings 'binop("udiv"' src/compiler/nir`), but this helper lowers the quotient to `fdiv`/`frcp` without a zero check. For example `umod x, 0` now becomes `x - 0 * ftrunc(x / 0)`, which can produce NaN/Inf on the no-integer backends this pass targets instead of the specified 0; previously these ops were not lowered at all, so this incorrect runtime result is introduced by the new cases.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Scalarize new udiv before emitting frcp**

For a vector `udiv` on Lima, this new path emits a vector `frcp` after Lima's last integer-op scalarization pass. I checked `src/gallium/drivers/lima/lima_program.c`: the filter explicitly scalarizes `nir_op_idiv` because `nir_lower_int_to_float` later turns it into `frcp`, but it does not include `nir_op_udiv`, and both Lima VS/FS call `nir_lower_int_to_float` afterward without another `nir_lower_alu_to_scalar`. That means shaders using `uvecN` division can now reach the Lima backend with the unsupported vector reciprocal shape that the existing `idiv` special case was avoiding.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Match the zero constant to imod bit size**

For `imod` values that are not 32-bit, this constructs a 32-bit float zero and then uses it in the `flt`/`bcsel` chain with `r` and `y`. `nir_imm_float()` is hardwired to 32-bit (checked in `src/compiler/nir/nir_builder.h` via `rg --fixed-strings 'nir_imm_float(' src/compiler/nir`), while `nir_op_imod` is an unsized int op, so 16-bit or 64-bit `imod` lowered by this pass will create mixed-bit-size ALU sources and fail NIR validation or backend assumptions instead of preserving the original bit size.

When any command buffer in the submit needs the multi-tile path, `inorder_host` is false for the whole submit, so this newly added case is skipped here and only replayed later by `r300vk_replay_cpu_readback` after all GPU work has finished. In a valid sequence such as `EndQuery -> CmdCopyQueryPoolResults -> barrier -> draw/dispatch reading dstBuffer` in the same submit, the later GPU command still sees the old buffer contents because the transfer write is deferred past it. `r300vk_copy_query_pool_results()` maps the destination with `PIPE_MAP_WRITE` even in the case where the query is unavailable and neither PARTIAL nor WAIT nor WITH_AVAILABILITY are set, i.e. when it will not write any bytes. A write-only Gallium map is allowed to discard/replace the previous contents for that range, so mapping+unmapping without writing can still clobber the destination buffer. The bounds check before casting `byte_off` to `unsigned` should also ensure `byte_off + per_query` fits in 32-bit. Add an explicit `byte_off > UINT_MAX - per_query` style guard (similar to other mapping sites in this file).

nodes.body: r300vk_bind_descriptor_textures binds samplers from every bound descriptor set, but the shader-side sampler index is derived only from `binding` (descriptor set is ignored). If multiple descriptor sets contain the same `binding`, the later set can silently clobber the earlier one, producing incorrect sampling. Until set+binding are flattened in NIR, this path should be gated to the one supported descriptor set (typically set 0) to avoid wrong pixels.

Descriptor slots can legally contain a different type than the layout binding (r300vk_UpdateDescriptorSets can spill writes across bindings and relies on consumers to check slot->type). This code reads `desc->img.*` unconditionally, which can misinterpret a buffer descriptor as an image/sampler and crash or bind garbage. Check `desc->type` before consuming the union.

r300vk_sampler_state_from_vk doesn't propagate VkSamplerCreateInfo's border color into pipe_sampler_state. This will produce incorrect sampling for CLAMP_TO_BORDER samplers (and custom border colors), and also leaves max_anisotropy at 0 when anisotropy is disabled (other Gallium/Vulkan paths default this to 1). Map border color via vk_sampler_border_color_value and set a sane anisotropy default.

r300vk_CreateSampler returns VK_SUCCESS even if pipe->create_sampler_state fails (pipe_cso == NULL). That leaves a live VkSampler whose replay-side binding will always skip, and also hides OOM from the application. Treat a NULL CSO as out-of-host-memory and destroy the partially-created vk_sampler.

Combined-image-sampler bindings can legally be descriptor arrays (binding->count > 1), and NIR will assign consecutive sampler indices for array elements. This replay path binds only the first descriptor at bnd->offset and never binds additional array elements (binding+1, binding+2, ...), so sampling any element other than [0] will still read the unbound-sampler default.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind every descriptor in sampler arrays**

When a `COMBINED_IMAGE_SAMPLER` binding has `descriptorCount > 1`, this binds only `descriptors[bnd->offset]` to unit `binding`; however `nir_lower_samplers` adds a constant array index to `var->data.binding` (`src/compiler/nir/nir_lower_samplers.c:65-94`, found with `rg --fixed-strings "nir_lower_samplers" src/`), so a shader sampling `samplerArray[1]` reads unit `binding + 1`. That unit is never populated here, so descriptor-array sampling still returns the unbound sampler default even though the descriptor was written.

As a result, out-of-range samples with opaque black/white or integer border colors return transparent zero rather than the Vulkan sampler's requested border value.

Because callers invoke decl_io() repeatedly for the same locations, this produces multiple shader inputs/outputs with identical locations, which can lead to invalid NIR or incorrect IO mapping (and breaks the intent of finalize() assigning driver_location once per IO). Cache/reuse an existing variable for a given (mode, location) instead of always creating a new one.

decl_sampler() creates a new uniform sampler variable on every call, even for the same binding. This will emit duplicate sampler uniforms with the same binding, which is likely to confuse resource binding and/or fail NIR validation. Reuse an existing sampler var for the binding, and mark the binding as explicit when creating it.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Encode the high byte of uint DP4 results**

For admitted `f2u32(fdot(...))` kernels whose dot value is at least `2^24`, this RGBA8 carrier drops the high byte because alpha is always written as zero. The dispatcher then copies these four RT bytes directly into the uint output SSBO, so a valid result such as `16777216` is returned as `0` instead of `0x01000000`. The detector now admits the uint-output shape without proving the runtime operand range, so either the fourth byte needs to be encoded or the admission must reject values outside the 24-bit carrier contract.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve fdot2 input element stride**

For admitted `fdot2` kernels whose SSBOs are arrays of `vec2`/two-float records, this always wraps the input as 16-byte RGBA32F texels even though the shader's load offsets advance by 8 bytes per invocation under std430 layout. The replay then samples invocation `i` from byte offset `16*i` instead of `8*i`, skipping every other element and reading past the end for the tail of a tightly packed vec2 buffer. The input carrier needs to depend on `pl->dp4.components` (or the detector must only admit 16-byte-stride inputs).

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Truncate the dot before byte encoding**

For admitted `f2u32(fdot(...))` kernels with non-integral dot results, the shader encodes the fractional `dot` value directly instead of the integer value produced by `f2u32`. Because the RGBA8 RT quantizes these normalized channels, a dot such as `1.5` can be copied back as byte value `2` even though `uint(1.5)` should store `1`. The synthesized FS needs to floor/truncate the dot before decomposing it into bytes, or the detector must only admit integer-valued dot inputs.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

The dp4 replay path now requires the compute kernel to store `f2u32(fdot(...))`, but the synthesized FS encodes the raw float `dot` value into RGBA8 bytes. If `dot` has any fractional part (e.g. non-quantized inputs), this will round during UNORM8 conversion and can diverge from `f2u32` truncation semantics. Truncate the dot to an integer (round-toward-zero) before the byte-split so the replay matches the admitted NIR shape.

nodes.body: `r300vk_idm_total_invocations()` multiplies up to six 32-bit factors into a `uint64_t` without overflow checks. If the product overflows, it can wrap to a small non-zero value and incorrectly pass the `total_invocations > 2048*2048` guard at call sites, leading to under-sized replay grids instead of rejecting the dispatch as out-of-bounds. Consider making the multiplication overflow-safe and treating overflow as 0 invocations (so existing callers reject it).

This comment still states the replay path “fixes local_size = 1 … later generalization widens … to local_size > 1”, but this PR explicitly adds `r300vk_idm_total_invocations()` to account for `pl->local_size_{x,y,z}`. When the local size pushes `total_invocations` just past one row, e.g. `group_count_x=33` with `local_size_x=64` gives N=2112, the raster extent becomes 2048x2. The input/output paths still map `width * height * bpp` bytes (for example the identity/binary readbacks and input wrap use the padded rectangle) even though only N elements are valid and `r300vk_identity_map_copy_rows` copies only `total_invocations`. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle every advertised color attachment**

With `VK_KHR_dynamic_rendering` enabled, applications may use any `colorAttachmentCount` up to the device limit (`maxColorAttachments` is still 4), but this records only `pColorAttachments[0]`. A valid dynamic-rendering pass that clears or renders to attachment 1-3, or leaves slot 0 null and uses a later slot, will replay with only one cbuf and silently drop those attachment writes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the render-area origin for clears**

When `renderArea.offset` is non-zero, storing only `offset + extent` as the framebuffer size loses the origin. Replay later implements `loadOp == CLEAR` with `pipe->clear` over the whole recorded framebuffer, so a valid dynamic-rendering begin with a subrect such as `{offset=(32,32), extent=(64,64)}` clears pixels from the top-left up to the far corner instead of only the requested render area.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Record dynamic depth/stencil attachments**

The new extension path ignores `pRenderingInfo->pDepthAttachment` and `pStencilAttachment` entirely, while the device still advertises depth/stencil attachment format support. A valid dynamic-rendering pass with no color attachments and a depth attachment, or a depth `loadOp == CLEAR`, will replay with `zsbuf == NULL`, so depth clears/tests/writes are silently dropped.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use American spelling in new comments**

The root `AGENTS.md` requires American English spelling in new or modified source comments, but this newly added comment uses `colour`. Please use `color` consistently in these dynamic-rendering comments to keep the patch within the documented repository rules.
